transcription.notes: Scans are bound out of order (p.3, p.2, p.4, p.1) and hold two despatches, 24 Apr and 4 May 1620.

system.summary: Simple substitution on a 24-sign alphabet of Latin-looking signs, used for spans inside otherwise clear Dutch, with a 116-entry numeric nomenclator written in parentheses.
system.doubled_letters: written twice; ij written as two i-signs
system.notes: The key is DECODE R2118, from the same inventory number. Its m cell is off the photographed sheet; m was recovered from the letters as the 4-shaped sign. Nomenclator codes 37-45 are in a column cut off by the photograph's edge. DECODE's record note calls the signs zodiacal and alchemistic; they are not.

prior_solution.where: DECODE lists R2113 and R2115 as Non-decrypted and carries no plaintext for them; no edition of these two despatches found

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the target with /goal. No target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Pulled the DECODE metadata for R2113-R2118 through the JSON API and fetched the 15 page images with the session cookie; found R2118 is the key for the series and R2114 already marked Decrypted.
Read the alphabet table off the two key pages of R2118; the signs are Latin letter shapes standing for other letters (e = 7, r = d, s = z, n = t, t = long s).
Tested the alphabet on the first cipher words of R2113 p.2: arbeiden, tusschen, suspensie, de turcken.
Transcribed and deciphered the cipher spans of R2113 and R2115 from rotated crops, in two parallel passes.
The key's m cell is not on the photographed sheet; m was inferred as the 4-shaped sign and confirmed in becomen, met, mijn, vermogen, teenemael, geconformeert.
Read the nomenclator list off R2118 and resolved the codes used in the letters.

Code values check against context: [19] Buda, [62] Transylvania, [70] Spain, [3] Vizier Azem, [4] Capitan Bassa, [7] Mufti, [58] the States General, [43] the Emperor's ambassador. [50] does not fit its key line and stays open; 37-45 rest on inferred order.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the two readings (cipher spans deciphered in braces) and the key files; no sign-level transcription of the cipher spans exists, so the transcription points to the DECODE records' images

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): R2113_reading.md builds Dutch sentences (B); R2115_reading.md calls itself partial, and P2/P4 are strings of [...], {?...} and bare codes. R2115 relabelled decoded, not read; class read -> read in part; fraction_read unknown -> about 0.48 (words).

Re-read brief b28, step 1: DECODE R2113-R2115 and R2118 re-fetched with the cookie (b28_fetch.py): no DOC_ attachment, comment or plaintext on any record; R2114's 'Decrypted' status has no file. Web search for a printed edition of Haga's 1620 despatches: none found. The key is R2118, already in use.

R2115 all four pages read line by line from native-resolution crops (b28_strips.py, b28_crop.py); clear Dutch transcribed in full; 43 cipher spans decoded sign by sign with the R2118 alphabet (R2115_cipher_spans.tsv). Corrections to the old partial reading: winninge van tijt, alomme odieus, favoriseren, tot faveur regis Bohemiae, gedisponeert, Ungarie soude aennemen, vanden siaus (not paus), gediffereert, verhoepe, geinformeert, spel, bulleman. Page order corrected to P3, P4, P2, P1 (P4 'den Vizir, Mufti,' runs on to P2 'Choggia, ende Janitsaraga').

Word-by-word alignment (b28_haga_align.py): 43/43 cipher spans found in order in the reading body; 13 letters on look-alike alternates (l/s, n/t, p, o, u); m = 4 holds at every occurrence; no key value changed. Score of the reading body: 0.023 (modern Dutch list), 0.942 explicit holes. Reader's judgement: sentences hold. R2115 set read, grade B.

Consistency pass (cl): the read bar failed on a stale gap 'R2115: decoded, not read' (not-attempted), closed by the b28 re-read of 23 Oct 2026 (R2115 read, grade B; NOTES already said so). outcome.gaps now mirrors the NOTES Remaining gaps: codes [15], [46], [50] (no-key-material) and a few clear words (illegible).

outcome.method_basis: The key is DECODE R2118, filed in the same Nationaal Archief series (inv. nr. 6894) as the letters R2113-R2115; its alphabet and 116-code nomenclator were read off the two key pages and fitted at once (arbeiden, tusschen, suspensie).
outcome.notes: Both catalogued ciphertexts read in sense; a handful of short cipher words and the code [50] stay open, and the clear Dutch was read for sense rather than transcribed verbatim. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: R2115 decoded, not read; class read -> read in part. 23 Oct 2026 (b28): R2115 re-read in full from the images (two letters, page order P3, P4, P2, P1), all cipher spans decoded and aligned; read, grade B; class back to read. Open: codes [15], [46] (R2115) and [50] (R2113), no key material.

texts.label: R2113 pp. 3+2, Haga to the States General, Constantinople, 31 Mar 1620 (p. 1 is the clear close of 1 Feb 1620)
texts.summary: Cornelis Haga, Dutch ambassador at Constantinople, reports that the Porte would let Transylvania be resigned to Bethlen Gábor's brother, that Transylvania must keep good correspondence with Hungary, and that the Turks would think better of the Hungarians if they too elected a king of Bohemia; the Grand Vizier, Capitan Bassa and Mufti press him on whether the States mean to extend the truce with Spain, make peace or take up arms again. No sign-level transcription of the cipher spans exists; the reading gives them deciphered in braces, and the images are on the DECODE record.

reading_review.note: Line-numbered Dutch with cipher spans in braces; the argument about Hungary, Bohemia and the Porte builds in sentences with a few ? and unresolved codes (per-document B).

texts.label: R2115, Haga to the States General, Constantinople, 24 Apr and [4-7] May 1620 (two letters; images in the order P3, P4, P2, P1)
texts.summary: Two letters. 24 April: Bohemian and Hungarian commissioners from the Pressburg Easter diet received by the Grand Vizier and the Sultan; in cipher, nothing is more necessary than gaining time and that the Hungarian Estates elect and crown a new king; the letter of Bethlen Gábor printed at Cologne to make him odious is a forgery; Naples too exhausted to help the Emperor. May: Haga has turned the Grand Vizier and the chief lords in favour of the King of Bohemia and of Transylvania; the Porte's letters promise perpetual peace; order given to the Bassa of Buda to assist; the Vizier and Mufti urge Bethlen to accept the crown of Hungary; the honour belongs to the States General alone; the chiaus to the Emperor's ambassador is delayed, 'om het spel in Duijtslant ende Ungaria met sodanigen bulleman te verderven'; Polish ambassador, Cossacks, Tatar invasion of Poland expected.

reading_review.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b28): all four pages transcribed from the DECODE photographs, the 43 cipher spans (599 letters) decoded sign by sign with the R2118 key and aligned in order with the reading (R2115_cipher_spans.tsv, b28_haga_align.py); 13 letters rest on a look-alike alternate. Clean-sentence share 0.023 on the modern Dutch list, 0.942 on explicit holes (b17_score.py HOLES=1); every sentence builds, scattered [?] words and codes [15], [46] open.

outcome.fraction_read_source: Estimated, reading audit 22 Oct 2026, by words of the two reading files: R2113_reading.md (1,249 words) reads, R2115_reading.md (1,337) is decoded, not read: 0.48. No token count of the cipher spans exists. The field was "unknown" before. 23 Oct 2026 (b28): R2115 now reads as well as R2113, so both catalogued documents read (1.0 by documents' words).
